clf-avc-040.text: A company wants a clear financial history of AWS spending over time and needs interactive filtering to understand which services and accounts are driving cost increases. Which AWS tool best fits this analysis?
options: AWS Cost Explorer
AWS Pricing Calculator
AWS Budgets
AWS Artifact
clf-avc-040.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive historical cost and usage analysis with filtering, grouping, and forecasting capabilities.
clf-avc-040.hint: Think of the AWS console tool for exploring actual historical spending rather than estimating a future architecture.
optionRationales: Cost Explorer analyzes actual cost and usage history.
Pricing Calculator estimates hypothetical future architecture costs.
Budgets focuses on thresholds and alerts rather than detailed historical exploration.
Artifact provides compliance reports and agreements, not cost analysis.

clf-avc-041.text: A retail company wants every AWS resource to be associated with business metadata such as department, project, and environment so finance can allocate cloud spending accurately. Which practice should be adopted?
options: Activate and use cost allocation tags consistently across resources.
Store project names only in CloudTrail event descriptions.
Use Security Groups as financial labels.
Separate costs exclusively by Availability Zone.
clf-avc-041.explanation: Cost allocation tags provide a consistent way to classify AWS resources and attribute spending to departments, projects, products, or environments.
clf-avc-041.hint: The requirement is financial attribution using metadata attached to resources.
optionRationales: Cost allocation tags enable showback and chargeback by business dimension.
CloudTrail records API actions and is not a resource cost-labeling system.
Security Groups control network access rather than financial classification.
Availability Zone location does not replace project and department cost metadata.

clf-avc-042.text: A global application needs a design that remains available if a single EC2 instance fails. Which architecture best reflects cloud reliability principles?
options: Run multiple instances across isolated failure domains behind a load balancer.
Run one very large EC2 instance with no redundancy.
Store all application state only on Instance Store.
Disable health checks to avoid automatic replacement.
clf-avc-042.explanation: Reliable architectures avoid single points of failure by distributing redundant capacity across isolated failure domains and routing traffic only to healthy targets.
clf-avc-042.hint: Reliability comes from redundancy and automated recovery rather than depending on one oversized server.
optionRationales: Multiple healthy targets across failure domains reduce single points of failure.
One large instance remains a single point of failure.
Instance Store is ephemeral and should not be the only location for critical persistent state.
Health checks enable automated detection and recovery rather than reducing reliability.

clf-avc-043.text: An organization wants to evaluate AWS resources automatically against best practices and receive recommendations covering areas such as cost, security, resilience, and performance. Which AWS tool provides this advisory capability?
options: AWS Trusted Advisor
Amazon Route 53
AWS CloudTrail
AWS Direct Connect
clf-avc-043.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor evaluates supported account resources and provides recommendations based on AWS best practices across several operational categories.
clf-avc-043.hint: Think of the automated AWS advisor that reviews the account and presents optimization recommendations.
optionRationales: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations for supported resources.
Route 53 provides DNS services.
CloudTrail records API activity but is not a best-practice advisor.
Direct Connect provides dedicated network connectivity.

clf-avc-044.text: A company wants to use AWS Trusted Advisor to understand whether its private on-premises data center is overprovisioned and to make automatic hardware changes there. Which limitation is important?
options: Trusted Advisor evaluates supported AWS-account resources and does not natively audit private on-premises infrastructure or automatically redesign customer hardware.
Trusted Advisor can modify any customer data-center hardware through the internet.
Trusted Advisor works only with Amazon S3 and no other AWS services.
Trusted Advisor is a replacement for all monitoring and security services.
clf-avc-044.explanation: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations about supported AWS resources. It does not natively inspect private on-premises infrastructure or automatically redesign hardware environments.
clf-avc-044.hint: Trusted Advisor is an AWS-account advisory tool, not a remote administrator for private data centers.
optionRationales: Its scope is supported AWS resources and advisory recommendations.
It cannot remotely control arbitrary physical hardware in a customer facility.
Its supported checks span multiple AWS service areas, not only S3.
It complements rather than replaces specialized monitoring and security services.

clf-avc-045.text: A mobile game company wants to launch a machine-learning matchmaking feature. With AWS, the team can create several identical test environments in minutes, compare models, and discard unsuccessful experiments without large fixed investments. Which cloud business benefit does this demonstrate?
options: Automatic freezing of operating costs regardless of usage.
Guaranteed zero latency for every user worldwide.
Agility and rapid experimentation with low financial risk.
Exclusive customer control of physical cloud hardware security.
clf-avc-045.explanation: Cloud agility lets teams provision advanced services on demand, test hypotheses, fail quickly, and remove unsuccessful environments without large upfront infrastructure investment.
clf-avc-045.hint: Focus on rapid experimentation and the ability to fail cheaply.
optionRationales: Agility enables rapid low-risk experimentation.
Physical infrastructure security is AWS's responsibility.
AWS costs vary with consumption rather than being automatically fixed.
Global infrastructure reduces latency but cannot guarantee zero network latency.
